# Visually Hidden

**Figma:** No Figma component: an accessibility primitive; a focused skip link is a Surface pill (Body/Base/Medium, Border/Neutral/Subtle ring, Focus/Accent outline)  
**Import:** `import { VisuallyHidden } from "@zen-ds/react";`

Adds text that only assistive technology reads: names for icon-only table headers, context for repeated links, status announcements, hidden headings and skip links that appear on focus.

## Use it for
- Column headers that show only an icon or nothing (Actions, Starred).
- Context that makes repeated labels unique ("Read more about …", "Edit email").
- Status messages for changes shown only visually (role="status": "Link copied to the clipboard").
- Skip links (as="a" + focusable) and headings that name a region for screen-reader navigation.

## Use something else for
- Naming an icon-only button → IconButton aria-label (it also shows the name as a tooltip).
- Naming a field → its label, or aria-label when the context labels it.
- Hiding content from everyone → don't render it.
- Hiding decoration from screen readers → aria-hidden.

## Figma → React
| Figma | Prop | Values / notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| — | `as` | span (default, inline) · div · p · label · legend · a · h1–h6 |
| — | `focusable` | shows the content while it, or a link inside it, has focus: a Surface pill at the top-start corner (skip links) |
| — | `href · htmlFor` | with as="a" · with as="label" |
| — | `role · aria-live · id` | role="status" for announcements; id for aria-labelledby / aria-describedby |

## Props
Generated from the TypeScript source; full JSON in `docs/api/visually-hidden.json`.

### VisuallyHidden
Content for assistive technology only. It is clipped to a 1px box (no layout impact) but stays in the accessibility tree, so screen readers read it and in-page search finds it. Use it to name icon-only table headers, add context to repeated links ("Read more about …"), announce status (role="status") and build skip links (`focusable`). No Figma node: this is an accessibility primitive with no visual design until a focusable one receives focus. `<VisuallyHidden>`Actions`</VisuallyHidden>` <VisuallyHidden as="a" href="#main" focusable>Skip to main content`</VisuallyHidden>`

Also accepts `HTMLAttributes<HTMLElement>`.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `as` | `"span" \| "div" \| "p" \| "label" \| "legend" \| "a" \| "h1" \| "h2" \| "h3" \| "h4" \| "h5" \| "h6"` | `"span"` | Element to render. Default span: inline, so it is valid inside buttons, links and table headers. Use div or p for a block, h2–h6 for a heading that names a region only screen readers need, label (with htmlFor) for a hidden field label, and a (with href and focusable) for a skip link. |
| `focusable` | `boolean` | `false` | Shows the content while it, or a link or button inside it, has focus: a Surface pill (Body/Base/Medium, Subtle ring) at the top-start corner of the nearest positioned ancestor, above the page. Use it for skip links. Default false. |
| `href` | `string` | — | With `as="a"`: the link target, e.g. "#main". |
| `htmlFor` | `string` | — | With `as="label"`: the id of the control it labels. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | — | The text for assistive technology (and for the visible pill while a focusable one has focus). |

## Keyboard
| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Tab (first stop on the page) | Show the focusable skip link |
| Enter | Follow the skip link; focus moves to the main content |

## ✅ Do
- Start hidden text that continues a visible label with a space and no punctuation (`Edit`<VisuallyHidden>` email`</VisuallyHidden>``) so the name reads as one phrase.
- Render a status region from the start, empty, then change its text; a region inserted together with its message is often not announced.
- Make the skip link the first focusable element of the page and point it at the main content (`tabIndex={-1}`).
- Keep the visible label inside the accessible name (WCAG 2.5.3): add words, never replace them.

## ❌ Don't
- Don't hide a link or control without focusable; keyboard users would land on something invisible (harness: visually-hidden/focusable-shows).
- Don't stuff keywords or long instructions into hidden text; screen-reader users hear every word.
- Don't use display:none, visibility:hidden or the hidden attribute for screen-reader text; they remove it from the accessibility tree.
- Don't hide a heading sighted people need too; show it.

## Accessibility
- The text is clipped to a 1px box (clip-path) and taken out of the flow, but stays in the accessibility tree and in-page search.
- Browsers insert a space before out-of-flow text when they build a name, so begin the hidden part with a space.
- A focused skip link shows a Surface pill with a Subtle ring and the Focus/Accent outline (WCAG 2.4.1 Bypass Blocks, 2.4.7 Focus Visible).

## Content
- Write hidden text as it will be heard: "Actions", " about Choosing a paper for photo prints", "Link copied to the clipboard".

## Harness (`npm run usage:check`)
| Rule | Severity | Checks | Suppress with |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `visually-hidden/focusable-shows` | error | Hidden content that takes keyboard focus (a skip link, a button) needs focusable, so it becomes visible while focused (WCAG 2.4.7). | `zen-allow-hidden-focus: <reason>` |
| `interaction/no-noop-handler` | warn | Every interaction a Zen control offers works: no no-op handlers (`() => {}`, `() => undefined`), which leave a field that ignores typing and ↑/↓ or a Dismiss that stays. Chat has chat/no-locked-interaction. | `zen-allow-noop-handler: <reason>` |
